2026-12-02.title: Wednesday after the Sunday of the Visitation
readings: How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news
Let your word be Yes or No
2026-12-02.alt: The Twenty-Five Days' Fast before Yaldo (Christmas), 1–24 December: prayer, fasting and almsgiving.
2026-12-02.verse: And how are they to proclaim him unless they are sent? As it is written, “How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news!”
theo: Paul builds a chain: people cannot call on one they have not believed in, cannot believe in one they have not heard of, cannot hear without a preacher, and there are no preachers unless they are sent. So the Church sends, and the feet of those who bring good news are beautiful. In this season before Christmas, every Christian is sent to announce that the Saviour comes.

Jesus asks for a simple, truthful tongue. Do not swear by heaven or earth or Jerusalem or your own head. “Let your word be ‘Yes, Yes’ or ‘No, No’; anything more than this comes from the evil one.” The messenger of the Word made flesh must be a person whose word can be trusted. Our fasting purifies the tongue as well as the stomach.
outline: “Let your word be ‘Yes, Yes’ or ‘No, No’.”
live: Speak only the truth today, even in small things.
Share one sentence of faith with someone this week.
2026-12-02.prayer: Lord Jesus, you send us to bring good news. Purify our tongues, make our yes and no truthful, and make our feet beautiful on the mountains of this world. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbono we hear the good news proclaimed. We receive the Word made flesh, and are sent out with beautiful feet.

quick: Faith comes through those who are sent.
The feet of messengers are beautiful.
Let your yes be yes and your no be no.
2026-12-02.action: Speak only the truth today, even in small things.
2026-12-02.question: Where do I bend the truth?

family.explain: Jesus wants our yes to mean yes and our no to mean no. When we always tell the truth, people can trust us.
family.intention: We pray that our family may always be honest.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there a promise we made that we need to keep?”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you are the truth. As we gather, make our words honest and our feet beautiful with the good news. Amen.
share: Paul asks: how will they hear without someone to proclaim? (Romans 10:14). Who first told me about Jesus?
Jesus says: let your yes be yes (Matthew 5:37). Where am I not fully honest?
To whom can I bring good news this week?
pm.resp: Lord, make us messengers of your truth.
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim the good news with joy.
For catechists and Sunday school teachers.
For those who have never heard of Christ, that someone may bring them the good news.
For those who live by lies and deceit, that they may turn to the truth.
For our families, that our words may be trustworthy.
pm.close: Lord God, how beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news. Make us honest in all our words and faithful messengers of your Son. Amen.

illus: A shopkeeper in Thiruvalla was known in the whole market for one thing: “If he says yes, it is yes.” Many customers who were not Christians said they first respected the Church because of him.

homily: Dear friends, St Paul asks a chain of questions: how are they to call on one in whom they have not believed? How are they to believe in one of whom they have never heard? How are they to hear without someone to proclaim him? And he answers with Isaiah: how beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news (Romans 10:14–15).
Faith comes through proclamation. Someone told us about Jesus: a mother, a catechist, a priest, a friend. Now it is our turn. The Lord wants beautiful feet that carry good news to others.

In the Gospel Jesus speaks about honesty: do not swear at all. Let your word be yes, yes or no, no; anything more than this comes from the evil one (Matthew 5:34, 37). A disciple does not need oaths, because his ordinary word can be trusted.

These two readings go together. The best proclamation of the Gospel is a truthful life. If our words at work, at home and on social media are not trustworthy, our words about Jesus will not be believed either.
In Kerala we sometimes swear casually: on God, on our mother, on the Bible. Jesus asks for something simpler and harder: be honest always, so that your yes is enough.

During this fast, let us examine our speech. Do I exaggerate, deceive, make promises I do not keep? Let us fast from lies and half-truths, and let our feet carry good news to someone who has not heard it. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus wants us to tell the truth always. When you say yes, mean it; when you promise, keep it!

sub: Jeremiah protested he was only a boy.
Paul: how will they hear without a preacher?
q: But the LORD said to me, “Do not say, ‘I am only a boy’; for you shall go to all to whom I send you, and you shall speak whatever I command you.
But how are they to call on one in whom they have not believed? And how are they to believe in one of whom they have never heard? And how are they to hear without someone to proclaim him?

sub: The law demanded that vows be kept.
Jesus asks for a plain yes or no.
q: When a man makes a vow to the LORD, or swears an oath to bind himself by a pledge, he shall not break his word; he shall do according to all that proceeds out of his mouth.
Let your word be ‘Yes, Yes’ or ‘No, No’; anything more than this comes from the evil one.

sub: Lying lips are an abomination to God.
q: Lying lips are an abomination to the LORD, but those who act faithfully are his delight.

concl: Messengers of the Word must be truthful.
Let the fast purify our tongues.
